text:
anya: quick RFC follow-up — i'm sketching a small ops API to prune stale precision variants from the quant-profile store. goal: shrink profile footprint, speed selection, and make profile canonicalization deterministic. thinking name `quant-profile-prune`. thoughts?
kevin: high level +1, but main concern is accidental quality regressions. what are the safety knobs? :thinking:
liam: we should include a conservative `degradation_budget` per-prune call and a `dry_run` mode that reports predicted quality impact and candidate list. also consider `min_usage` and `min_tokens` filters so we don't nuke long-tail but still-important profiles.
sara: must have an automated evaluation step. before removing profile X, run a tiny shadow eval on a representative prompt set and fail prune if delta > threshold. add audit logs and an undo record.
devex-bot: shared doc with a prototype sketch: <https://redwood-internal/quant/prune-design> :eyes:
anya: rough API idea:```POST /v1/quant/profiles/{model}/prune{ "dry_run": true, "degradation_budget": 0.015, "max_candidates": 500, "filters": {"min_usage_days": 30, "shapes": ["512x1024"]} }```response lists candidate profiles + estimated delta (shadow eval) + confidence.
kevin: nice. add `per_tenant_override: true/false` so enterprise customers can opt-out of auto-prunes. we need immutable tombstones so runtime can fallback to killed profiles if a rollback is necessary.
liam: implementation notes: operate on profile metadata only (no model recompile), use an offline batch job that ranks by stale_score = alpha*1/age + beta*usage_decay + gamma*quality_risk. prune engine emits curated manifest with hashes. runtime will consult manifest and a `prune-safe` flag at selection time.
sara: ops checklist: (1) unit tests for ranking, (2) shadow-eval harness (3) canary prune on 1% traffic, (4) 24h regression watch, (5) auto-rollback. we should wire alerts to #eng-oncall and perf dashboards.
anya: proposed rollout: week1 dry_run + manual review; week2 staged pruning on non-prod models; week3 canary on <5% traffic; week4 ramp. owners: liam (engine), kevin (runtime), sara (qa), anya (spec + rollout).
kevin: logging: store per-prune artifact with list of removed profile ids, shadow-eval diffs, and link to artifact. make it queryable by customer id.
liam: for determinism, canonicalize profiles by `(model, shape, quant-spec, hash)` and use a compact bloom filter for runtime lookup to keep selection fast. migrate old profiles by running `profile:canonicalize` job first.
sara: add a mandatory small eval-set per model (50 prompts) that every prune run must execute. shadow eval should run in parallel and finish within pruning window or abort.
anya: agree. also adding `rollback_window_seconds` and `tombstone_reason` fields to API. sample call for admin usage:```curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://api.redwood/v1/quant/profiles/gpt-open-3/prune -d '{"dry_run":false, "degradation_budget":0.01, "max_candidates":200, "filters":{"min_usage_days":90}}'```
kevin: fine, but add rate-limit to prevent accidental mass-prunes. and ensure Dedicated/Private customers are respected.
opsbot: deploybot: scheduled a staging job `quant-prune-canary` for 2024-09-12T03:20:00Z. logs will be in /var/log/prune-canary/1761234568.log :hammer:
anya: next steps: i'll open a tiny RFC PR with the API surface, sample responses, and the strict opt-out semantics. tagging owners above. thanks all :thumbsup:
